name: Lust and Pornography

counsel.text: Set faith at work on Christ for the killing of thy sin. His blood is the great sovereign remedy for sin-sick souls. Live in this, and thou wilt die a conqueror; yea, thou wilt, through the good providence of God, live to see thy lust dead at thy feet.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: Sin aims always at the utmost; every time it rises up to tempt or entice, might it have its own course, it would go out to the utmost sin in that kind. Every unclean thought or glance would be adultery if it could; every covetous desire would be oppression, every thought of unbelief would be atheism, might it grow to its head.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 2

counsel.text: Know that he that dares to dally with occasions of sin will dare to sin. He that will venture upon temptations unto wickedness will venture upon wickedness.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: For the provision to be laid up, it is that which is provided in the gospel for us. Gospel provisions will do this work; that is, keep the heart full of a sense of the love of God in Christ. This is the greatest preservative against the power of temptation in the world.
counsel.author: John Owen

counsel.text: The eye tempts the fancy, and the fancy works upon the heart. A wanton amorous eye may usher in sin. Eve first saw the tree of knowledge, and then she took. Gen 3: 6. First she looked and then she loved.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the seventh commandment

counsel.text: To lascivious books I may add lascivious pictures, which bewitch the eye, and are incendiaries to lust. They secretly convey poison to the heart.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the seventh commandment

counsel.text: The best course to prevent falling into the pit, is to keep at the greatest distance; he that will be so bold as to attempt to dance upon the brink of the pit, may find by woful experience that it is a righteous thing with God that he should fall into the pit. Joseph keeps at a distance from sin, and from playing with Satan's golden baits, and stands. David draws near, and plays with the bait, and falls, and swallows bait and hook with a witness.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks

counsel.text: Poor man sins upon Satan's credit, and receives it into his bosom, as Jacob did his wife into his bed—before he sees its face, or knows well what it is—and therefore, as he in the morning found her to be, not that beautiful Rachel as was promised, but a blear-eyed Leah; so the sinner, too late—when his conscience awakes—sees himself miserably cheated, and disappointed of what he looked for, and finds a purgatory where he expected a paradise.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: It is like, thou wouldst not be seen to walk in the street with such company—not lead a whore by the hand through the town—not violently break open thy neighbour's house to murder or rob him; but canst thou not under thy own roof, in the withdrawing room of thy soul, let thy thoughts hold up an unclean lust, while thy heart commits speculative folly with it?
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: As he tempts the devil to tempt him that lets his eyes gaze, or thoughts gad, upon a lustful object, so he bespeaks the Holy Spirit's company that lets out his thoughts upon holy heavenly objects. We need not doubt but the Spirit of God is as willing to cherish any good motion, as the infernal spirit is to nourish that which is evil.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: Where the Spirit is, it is such a light as discovers not only dunghills, but motes themselves, even light and flying imaginations, and abaseth the soul for them, and by degrees purgeth them out; and if they press, as they are as busy as flies in summer, yet a good heart will not own them, nor allow himself in them, but casts them off, as hot water doth the scum, or as the stomach doth that which is noisome unto it.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 13

counsel.text: The eye is the window of the soul, and if that should be always open, the soul might smart for it. A man may not look intently upon that, that he may not love entirely. The disciples were set a-gog, by beholding the beauty of the temple. It is best and safest to have the eye always fixed upon the highest and noblest objects: as the mariner's eye is fixed upon the star, when their hand is on the stern.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.opening: Holy, holy, holy Lord God, your eyes are too pure to look on evil, and nothing in me is hidden from you; yet you are my Father, and I bless you that I may come to you through Jesus Christ, your Son.
prayers.text: I confess that I have sinned against you with my eyes, my thoughts, and my body. I have looked where I should have turned away. I have fed desires you forbid, and I have treated another person, made in your image, as a thing for my pleasure. I have gone looking for comfort, escape, and power in a counterfeit, when you offered me yourself. Against you, you only, have I sinned. I have grieved your Holy Spirit and dishonored the body that belongs to you. I do not only want to be rid of the shame; teach me to hate this sin because it is against you and against your love. I have no plea in myself. But Christ bore this very sin in his body on the tree, and his blood cleanses from all sin. He lives to intercede for me. For his sake, forgive me and wash me. Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. By your Spirit put this lust to death at its root, and give me a greater delight in you than in any pleasure of sin. Keep me from ever calling it small again.
prayers.closing: I thank you that there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. To him who loves me and has freed me from my sins by his blood be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.

prayers.title: In the hour of temptation
prayers.opening: Holy Father, I flee to you now, through Jesus, my great High Priest, at the throne of grace.
prayers.text: Lord Jesus, you were tempted in every way as I am, yet without sin, and you know how fierce this hour is. I will not hide it from you. Help me now. Do not let me give this thought one more moment, or take one more look. Turn my eyes from worthless things, and give me strength to get up and go. Remind me that my body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, and that I was bought with a price, your own blood. Show me again the joy that is in you, greater than this passing pleasure. Holy Spirit, by your power put to death what is rising in me.
prayers.closing: I belong to you. To you, who are able to keep me from falling, be glory for ever. Amen.

prayers.title: For a pure heart
prayers.opening: Beautiful and holy God, you are the fountain of all true joy, and you have promised that the pure in heart shall see you.
prayers.text: I want that blessing more than anything this world offers. Make my heart pure. Fill my mind with what is true, honorable, and lovely, so that there is no room left for what defiles. Teach me to see every man and woman as your image bearer, to honor them and never to use them. Guard my eyes, my hands, and my hours alone. Make me watchful over the occasions of sin, and quick to bring them into the light before trusted believers. Above all, satisfy me with your steadfast love, so that I do not hunger for counterfeits.
prayers.closing: Through Jesus Christ my Lord, my joy and my crown, to whom be glory for ever. Amen.

prayers.title: Confessing sensuality and flesh-pleasing
prayers.opening: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come.
prayers.text: We have minded the things of the flesh more than the things of the Spirit, and have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton, and have nourished our hearts as in a day of slaughter. We have made provision for the flesh to fulfil the lusts of it; even those lusts which war against our souls: and in many instances have acted as if we had been lovers of pleasure more than lovers of God.
prayers.closing: Now to God the Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father, be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry
prayers.source: arranged from A Method for Prayer, chs. 1, 2 and 7

prayers.title: That the flesh may be crucified in us
prayers.opening: Thou hast appointed us a great High Priest, in whose name we may come boldly to the throne of grace, that we may find mercy and grace to help in time of need.
prayers.text: O let no iniquity have dominion over us, because we are not under the law, but under grace. Let the flesh be crucified in us with its affections and lusts; that walking in the Spirit we may not fulfil the lusts of the flesh. Let our old man be crucified with Christ, that the body of sin may be destroyed, that henceforth we may not serve sin; and let not sin reign in our mortal bodies (in our immortal souls) that we should obey it in the lusts thereof. But being made free from sin, let us become the servants of righteousness. Let the law of the Spirit of life, which is in Christ Jesus, make us free from the law of sin and death. Give us grace to put off the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts, that we may put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.
prayers.closing: Now unto him that is able to keep us from falling, and to present us faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, to the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, now and ever. Amen.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry
prayers.source: arranged from A Method for Prayer, chs. 1, 3 and 7

examinationQuestions: When this desire stirred today, what were you seeking in it that you were not seeking from Christ: comfort, escape, rest, or to feel wanted?
What occasions of sin did you allow, such as a place, an hour, a device, or a thought you let linger, and where did you first turn toward it?
Do you grieve over this sin because it offends God and grieves his Spirit, or mostly because of the shame it brings you?
What does this sin whisper to you about God: that he does not see, or that he is keeping some good thing from you?
Have you thought of the people on the screen as someone's son or daughter, made in God's image and needing Christ, or only as things to use?
Have you brought this sin into the light with one of your brethren or your pastor, or are you still keeping it in the dark?
fleeActions: Put the phone or computer down now. Leave it in another room, and do not go back to it for at least an hour.
Get up and leave the place where you are. Go where other people are, or step outside and walk, and then take up the next duty in front of you.
Text or call one of your brethren now. Say plainly, "I am being tempted. Please pray for me."
Open a paper Bible, not a screen, and read Psalm 51 or Psalm 119:9-16 out loud.
If it is late, go to bed now. Leave every screen outside the room, and pray before you lie down.
Today, put a filter and accountability on every device you use, and give the passwords to someone you trust in your church.

afterFallReadings.text: Hast thou not often been ready to conclude thyself, that it was utterly impossible that he should bear any longer with thee; that he would cast thee off, and be gracious no more; that all his forbearance was exhausted, and hell and wrath was even ready prepared for thee? and yet, above all thy expectation, he hath returned with visitations of love.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

afterFallReadings.text: A soul steeped in the briny tears of repentance, and bathed in the blood of Christ, is made pure.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: The Ten Commandments, the seventh commandment

afterFallReadings.text: I also saw, moreover, that it was not my good frame of heart that made my righteousness better, nor yet my bad frame that made my righteousness worse; for my righteousness was Jesus Christ Himself, the same yesterday, and to-day, and for ever (Heb. 13.8).
afterFallReadings.author: John Bunyan
afterFallReadings.source: Grace Abounding to the Chief of Sinners, §229
